input_signals.name: Accrual-Stripped Enterprise Yield
input_signals.hypothesis: Enterprise earnings yield should predict stronger returns when EBITDA remains high after deducting investment in operating working capital.
input_signals.reasoning: Subtracting working-capital accruals from EBITDA produces a cash-conversion-adjusted operating yield rather than conditioning a published EBITDA/EV measure on a binary gate. The continuous ratio preserves cross-sectional ordering and avoids a zero mass while requiring both inexpensive enterprise value and limited accrual-funded earnings.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: rank( ratio( sub( ebitda, sub( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), sub( sub( delta( lct, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ), delta( txp, 1 ) ) ) ), add( add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), dltt ), sub( dlc, che ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Working-Capital-Ex Book Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that remain cheap after removing net operating working-capital balances from book equity should outperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This measure does not append a generic quality score to book-to-market; it directly removes current operating assets whose book values are especially exposed to receivable, inventory, and other accrual write-downs. Industry ranking controls for persistent differences in normal working-capital requirements while retaining broad level-data coverage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( ratio( sub( ceq, sub( sub( act, che ), sub( sub( lct, dlc ), txp ) ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) )

input_signals.name: Collected-Sales Value
input_signals.hypothesis: High sales-yield firms should outperform when receivables are decreasing and reported sales are converting into cash.
input_signals.reasoning: Compustat RECCH is positive when accounts receivable decrease, so the revised direction correctly treats high RECCH as evidence of collection rather than accumulation. The minimum operator requires both within-industry sales cheapness and favorable receivable conversion, producing a naturally positive signal instead of implicitly favoring expensive firms.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( sale, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( recch, at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Under-Depreciation Book Trap
input_signals.hypothesis: High book-to-market firms should underperform when their depreciation intensity is falling.
input_signals.reasoning: A decline in depreciation relative to assets can temporarily support reported income and book equity by reducing the accrual recognized for asset consumption. Interacting that policy change with book cheapness tests deterioration in the reliability of book value, rather than mechanically replacing EBITDA with EBIT.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( mul( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), neg( delta( ratio( dp, at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Accrual-Financing-Adjusted Earnings Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Earnings yield should predict stronger returns when the apparent valuation discount survives capitalization of incremental operating working-capital funding.
input_signals.reasoning: The denominator adds a charge only when operating working capital increases: for a negative change, the change plus its absolute value is zero. This avoids rewarding releases as extra earnings, excludes cash and short-term debt from the accrual measure, and treats accrual expansion as additional capital required to obtain the reported income stream.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( ratio( ib, add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), add( delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( sub( lct, dlc ), txp ) ), 1 ), abs( delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( sub( lct, dlc ), txp ) ), 1 ) ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Depreciation-Policy-Neutral Earnings Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms should outperform when earnings remain inexpensive after neutralizing changes in the depreciation provision.
input_signals.reasoning: A decline in depreciation can mechanically support current income, so adding the negative depreciation change back to income reduces the valuation numerator; an increase receives the opposite adjustment. This converts the previously successful under-depreciation trap mechanism into a continuous, positively oriented yield without merely substituting EBIT for EBITDA.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( ratio( add( ib, delta( dp, 1 ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Composition Book Value
input_signals.hypothesis: High book-to-market firms should outperform when a large share of current assets consists of cash rather than accrual-sensitive operating assets.
input_signals.reasoning: The cash share of current assets measures the realizability of the balance-sheet assets supporting book value, directly reducing exposure to receivable and inventory write-down risk. This level-based construction uses broadly available balance-sheet data instead of sacrificing coverage to remove a typically negligible tax cash-flow item.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( mul( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ratio( che, act ) ) )

input_signals.name: Accrual-Overhang-Adjusted Earnings Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Earnings yield should predict stronger returns when cheapness survives a charge for operating working capital accumulated above its recent low-water mark.
input_signals.reasoning: The distance from the three-period minimum measures unreversed accrual capital still tied up in current operations, rather than another one-period Sloan accrual. Adding that nonnegative overhang to the effective purchase price filters firms whose inexpensive earnings require a persistently elevated operating-asset commitment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( ratio( ib, add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sub( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( sub( lct, dlc ), txp ) ), ts_min( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( sub( lct, dlc ), txp ) ), 3 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Noncash-Capital Enterprise Yield
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms should outperform when EBITDA remains inexpensive after including noncash current assets in the capital required to acquire and operate the business.
input_signals.reasoning: The denominator treats receivables, inventories, and other noncash current assets as additional operating capital rather than applying a positive multiplier to potentially negative earnings. This produces a monotone enterprise yield and tests whether operating cheapness survives the capital tied up in accrual-sensitive assets.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( ratio( ebitda, add( add( add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), dltt ), sub( dlc, che ) ), sub( act, che ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Depreciation-Reserved Cash Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms should outperform when operating cash flow remains inexpensive after treating depreciation and amortization addbacks as an economic reserve.
input_signals.reasoning: DPC is used directly as a material noncash addback rather than being differenced against the nearly equivalent DP definition. Subtracting it from operating cash flow asks whether cash-flow cheapness survives a conservative allowance for asset consumption, avoiding the zero-heavy reclassification residual.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( ratio( sub( oancf, dpc ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) )

input_signals.name: Accrual-Capitalized Sales Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms should outperform when sales remain inexpensive after capitalizing positive net operating working capital into the effective purchase price.
input_signals.reasoning: Net operating working capital plus its absolute value is positive only for firms requiring accrual capital and zero for negative-working-capital firms. The construction therefore preserves monotonicity in sales yield, penalizes asset-heavy operating models without reversing the ordering, and does not mechanically reward the published operating-liability-leverage effect.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( ratio( sale, add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), add( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( sub( lct, dlc ), txp ) ), abs( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( sub( lct, dlc ), txp ) ) ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Short-Debt-Covered Book Value
input_signals.hypothesis: High book-to-market firms should outperform when cash also provides strong coverage of short-term debt relative to current assets.
input_signals.reasoning: Cash composition is less reassuring when the cash is effectively claimed by near-term borrowing, so netting DLC from cash turns the quality channel into a liquidity-survival test. The conjunctive ranking remains monotone in book cheapness and prevents highly leveraged value firms from scoring well solely because they report substantial gross cash.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sub( che, dlc ), act ) ) )

input_signals.name: Binding Accrual-Overhang Value
input_signals.hypothesis: High earnings yield should predict stronger returns only when unreversed operating working-capital accumulation is low.
input_signals.reasoning: The earlier effective-price adjustment delivered a strong cross-sectional slope but only modest abnormal-return reliability because the overhang was often small relative to market value. Making the temporal accounting state a separate binding hurdle prevents plain earnings yield from dominating and concentrates the long portfolio in genuinely low-overhang value firms.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( ib, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( sub( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( sub( lct, dlc ), txp ) ), ts_min( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( sub( lct, dlc ), txp ) ), 3 ) ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Depreciation-Covered Cash Value
input_signals.hypothesis: High operating-cash-flow yield should predict stronger returns only when cash flow remains robust after a depreciation and amortization reserve.
input_signals.reasoning: Separating valuation from reserve coverage makes DPC a binding accounting-quality hurdle instead of merely changing the denominator of the previously successful equity yield. The construction avoids negative enterprise values and requires both inexpensive cash flow and positive residual cash profitability relative to assets.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( oancf, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sub( oancf, dpc ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Working-Capital-Stable Operating Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Operating earnings cheapness should predict stronger returns when net operating working-capital intensity is stable.
input_signals.reasoning: A separate quality hurdle ensures that accounting stability materially affects the ordering rather than entering as a small denominator adjustment. Using one absolute first change avoids a noisy three-observation volatility estimate, while the gross equity-plus-debt valuation base remains positive and reduces unstable portfolio composition.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( ebitda, add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), add( dltt, dlc ) ) ) ), ind_rank( neg( abs( delta( ratio( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( sub( lct, dlc ), txp ) ), at ), 1 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Rising-Liquidity Earnings Value
input_signals.hypothesis: High earnings-yield firms should outperform when the cash share of current assets is rising persistently.
input_signals.reasoning: A rising cash share provides balance-sheet evidence that operating accrual assets are converting into liquidity, without relying on sparsely reported RECCH. The three-period trend changes the mechanism from a recycled collection hurdle to persistent liquidity improvement while retaining broad ACT and CHE coverage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( ib, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ind_rank( trend( ratio( che, act ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Seasoned-Depreciation Book Value
input_signals.hypothesis: High book-to-market firms should outperform when their asset base has absorbed substantial cumulative depreciation and amortization.
input_signals.reasoning: Cumulative depreciation provides a stock-consistent measure of how much accounting cost has already been recognized against the assets supporting book equity. This replaces the single-field substitution in the cash-flow signal with a distinct book-value reliability mechanism and avoids making OANCF the coverage bottleneck.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( dp, 3 ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Accrual-Loaded Loss Trap
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms should underperform when large accounting losses relative to market value coincide with a persistent operating working-capital overhang.
input_signals.reasoning: This formulation focuses directly on the negative-earnings firms excluded from the successful positive overhang signal rather than substituting another valuation numerator. A high score requires both a loss yield and unreversed accrual capital, isolating firms burning earnings while cash remains tied up in current operations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( neg( ib ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sub( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( sub( lct, dlc ), txp ) ), ts_min( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( sub( lct, dlc ), txp ) ), 3 ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Depreciation-Honest Earnings Value
input_signals.hypothesis: High earnings yield should predict stronger returns when depreciation intensity is increasing rather than being cut to support income.
input_signals.reasoning: Ranking the depreciation change separately prevents market capitalization from dominating the accounting-policy measure and aligns cheapness with the expected-return direction. The high tail contains profitable value firms whose earnings remain inexpensive despite a strengthening depreciation provision, rather than firms made artificially cheap by a depreciation cut.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( ib, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ind_rank( delta( ratio( dp, at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Noncash-Asset-Turnover Earnings Value
input_signals.hypothesis: High earnings-yield firms should outperform when sales are generated with little capital tied up in noncash current assets.
input_signals.reasoning: Turnover of noncash current assets measures how efficiently receivables, inventories, and other accrual-sensitive assets support revenue. This replaces stacked accounting gates with a distinct operating-efficiency mechanism: reported earnings are more credible when the business requires fewer current accrual assets per dollar of sales.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( ib, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sale, sub( act, che ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Tax-Confirmed Earnings Value
input_signals.hypothesis: High earnings yield should predict stronger returns when tax payables are declining rather than accumulating.
input_signals.reasoning: A decline in taxes payable is consistent with reported profitability being accompanied by settlement of previously accrued tax obligations, whereas a buildup can preserve cash temporarily. Making the balance-sheet tax change a separate hurdle gives the tax-quality channel meaningful influence and avoids the sparse, economically negligible TXACH subtraction used previously.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( ib, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( delta( txp, 1 ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Scale-Stable Liquidity Conversion Value
input_signals.hypothesis: High earnings-yield firms should outperform when the cash share of current assets is rising without a large change in operating scale.
input_signals.reasoning: Subtracting the magnitude of sales growth penalizes both contraction-driven liquidation and unusually rapid expansion, rather than requiring top-ranked sales growth. A high quality score therefore represents conversion of accrual assets into cash within a relatively stable business, avoiding the adverse growth tilt of the previous specification.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( ib, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ind_rank( sub( trend( ratio( che, act ), 3 ), abs( growth( sale, 1 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Short-Debt-Funded Loss Trap
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms should underperform when large losses relative to market value coincide with increasing reliance on short-term debt.
input_signals.reasoning: Losses are more dangerous when they are financed through debt that must be refinanced quickly, creating a direct funding-runway mechanism rather than another inventory or working-capital anomaly. Requiring both a loss yield and growth in short-term debt focuses the high tail on financially fragile value traps.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( neg( ib ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( delta( dlc, 1 ), lct ) ) )

input_signals.name: Depreciation-Reserved Liability Coverage Value
input_signals.hypothesis: High operating-cash-flow yield should predict stronger returns when cash remaining after a depreciation reserve provides strong coverage of current liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: The second channel measures solvency after recognizing asset consumption, not persistence obtained by cosmetically smoothing the previously successful quality leg. This distinguishes genuinely distributable cash value from firms whose high cash-flow yield is offset by depreciation needs and near-term operating or financing claims.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( oancf, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sub( oancf, dpc ), lct ) ) )

input_signals.name: Working-Capital-Reversal Earnings Value
input_signals.hypothesis: High earnings-yield firms should outperform when net operating working capital has been released from a recent peak.
input_signals.reasoning: The successful low-water-mark signal measures accumulated overhang, whereas this construction measures an actual reversal catalyst from the recent maximum. A high score requires inexpensive positive earnings and realized release of capital previously tied up in current operations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( ib, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sub( ts_max( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( sub( lct, dlc ), txp ) ), 3 ), sub( sub( act, che ), sub( sub( lct, dlc ), txp ) ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Accrual-Haircut Net Cash Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms should outperform when cash net of short-term debt is valuable relative to equity price and the noncash current assets exposed to accrual risk.
input_signals.reasoning: The numerator measures immediately available liquidity after short-term borrowing, while the denominator treats noncash current assets as additional capital exposed to collection or write-down risk. This is a liquidation-cushion interaction rather than a swap between correlated earnings and cash-flow yield legs.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( ratio( sub( che, dlc ), add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sub( act, che ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Asset-Consumption Funding Deficit
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms should underperform when depreciation and amortization exceed operating cash flow by a large amount relative to equity value and current liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: A positive deficit indicates that operations are not generating enough cash to cover an accounting proxy for asset consumption, making apparent cheapness difficult to sustain. Pricing the deficit against equity plus near-term claims creates a trap-severity measure rather than smoothing or swapping legs of an existing cash-value signal.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( ratio( sub( dpc, oancf ), add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), lct ) ) )

input_signals.name: Collected-Sales Accrual-Capital Yield
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms should outperform when customer cash collections are high relative to both market value and noncash current assets required by the business.
input_signals.reasoning: Since positive RECCH denotes a receivable decrease, sales plus RECCH approximates cash collected from customers during the period. Comparing those collections with equity price plus noncash current assets jointly rewards inexpensive customer cash generation and low accrual-capital requirements without relying on the opaque AOLOCH item.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( ratio( add( sale, recch ), add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sub( act, che ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Liability-Neutral Operating Cash Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms should outperform when operating cash flow remains inexpensive after removing cash generated by increases in ordinary operating liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: Growth in nondebt, nontax current liabilities can temporarily boost operating cash through delayed payments, while liability runoff creates the opposite timing drag. Removing the signed balance-sheet change estimates cash generation before operating-liability financing, providing a broad-coverage quality adjustment rather than another value-anchor robustness check.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( ratio( sub( oancf, delta( sub( sub( lct, dlc ), txp ), 1 ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) )

input_signals.name: Turnover-Secured Net Cash Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Net-cash cheapness should predict stronger returns when noncash current assets convert rapidly through sales.
input_signals.reasoning: Both components are dimensionless: net cash relative to market value and sales relative to noncash current assets. The interaction avoids adding a liquidity stock to a historical release and instead tests whether a liquid valuation cushion is supported by a business that can efficiently realize its remaining accrual assets.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( mul( ratio( sub( che, dlc ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ratio( sale, sub( act, che ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Self-Financed Asset-Renewal Cash Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms should outperform when operating cash remains inexpensive after reserving for asset consumption and removing cash supplied by increases in operating liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: Subtracting DPC recognizes depreciation and amortization as an economic reserve, while subtracting the change in nondebt, nontax current liabilities removes cash generated by delayed operating payments. Unlike the prior construction, it does not add back the asset side of working capital and therefore does not algebraically collapse toward net income.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( ratio( sub( sub( oancf, dpc ), delta( sub( sub( lct, dlc ), txp ), 1 ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) )

input_signals.name: Low-Carry Earnings Value
input_signals.hypothesis: High earnings-yield firms should outperform when operating working capital and short-term debt impose a low carrying burden relative to sales.
input_signals.reasoning: Scaling the funding burden by sales separates operational capital intensity from the market-price effect that gave level-to-price congestion measures a positive slope. The positive orientation also prevents cheap, asset-heavy firms from being labeled return-negative merely because their market capitalization is low.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( ib, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( add( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( sub( lct, dlc ), txp ) ), dlc ), sale ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Accrual-Funded Dividend Trap
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms should underperform when dividends exceed operating cash remaining after a depreciation and amortization reserve.
input_signals.reasoning: The numerator measures the portion of the payout not covered by post-reserve operating cash, directly identifying dividends that may require borrowing, asset sales, or continued accrual financing. Non-payers do not create an artificial high-score mass, while the high tail isolates economically meaningful payout-value traps.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( ratio( sub( dvc, sub( oancf, dpc ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) )

input_signals.name: Customer-Neutral Asset-Renewal Cash Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms should outperform when operating cash remains inexpensive after reserving for depreciation and removing cash-flow effects from receivable changes.
input_signals.reasoning: Positive RECCH can temporarily raise operating cash through collection of prior-period receivables, while negative RECCH depresses cash through new customer financing. Subtracting the signed item isolates post-depreciation cash generation before receivable timing, distinguishing recurring operating value from cash flow produced by liquidating customer balances.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( ratio( sub( sub( oancf, dpc ), recch ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) )

input_signals.name: Creditor-Funded Dividend Trap
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms should underperform when dividends exceed post-depreciation operating cash while operating liabilities are increasing.
input_signals.reasoning: An uncovered payout is particularly fragile when the firm is simultaneously generating cash by delaying payments to suppliers and other operating creditors. The second hurdle identifies the funding source behind the dividend deficit, converting the payout shortfall from a standalone coverage measure into a creditor-financed value-trap mechanism.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( sub( dvc, sub( oancf, dpc ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( delta( sub( sub( lct, dlc ), txp ), 1 ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Loss-Making Accrual-Asset Congestion
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms should underperform when large losses relative to market value coincide with low turnover of noncash current assets.
input_signals.reasoning: Noncash current assets can be productive and value-supporting in profitable firms, which explains why the unconditional congestion signal had a positive average slope. Requiring a simultaneous loss yield isolates firms whose receivables, inventories, and other accrual assets are failing to generate sufficient sales while reported equity value is already impaired.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( neg( ib ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sub( act, che ), sale ) ) )
